Reading the results

Source: vignettes/results.Rmd
results.Rmd

A nested run returns a nested_results, a tibble with one row per outer fold. This page reads one run from start to finish: the estimate, what each fold selected, the predictions and the plots.

library(tidymodels)
library(nestedtune)

The run

We reuse the design, the random forest and the grid from vignette("nested-cv"). This time a control_grid() with save_pred = TRUE keeps each outer fold’s predictions on its assessment rows.

set.seed(1)

folds <- nested_resamples(
  mtcars,
  outside = vfold_cv(v = 5),
  inside = vfold_cv(v = 5)
)

rf <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 500) |>
  set_engine("ranger") |>
  set_mode("regression")

wf <- workflow(mpg ~ ., rf)

grid <- expand.grid(mtry = c(2L, 5L, 8L), min_n = c(2L, 10L))

set.seed(2)

res <- nested_tune_grid(
  wf,
  folds,
  grid = grid,
  control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE)
)

res
#> 
#> ── Nested cross-validation results ────────────────────────────────────
#> Outer resamples: 5-fold cross-validation
#> # A tibble: 5 × 10
#>   splits         id    .metrics .selected .inner_metrics    .notes  
#>   <list>         <chr> <list>   <list>    <list>            <list>  
#> 1 <split [25/7]> Fold1 <tibble> <tibble>  <tibble [12 × 8]> <tibble>
#> 2 <split [25/7]> Fold2 <tibble> <tibble>  <tibble [12 × 8]> <tibble>
#> 3 <split [26/6]> Fold3 <tibble> <tibble>  <tibble [12 × 8]> <tibble>
#> 4 <split [26/6]> Fold4 <tibble> <tibble>  <tibble [12 × 8]> <tibble>
#> 5 <split [26/6]> Fold5 <tibble> <tibble>  <tibble [12 × 8]> <tibble>
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: .predictions <list>, .completed <lgl>,
#> #   .tuning_seed <int>, .outer_fit_seed <int>
#> ℹ Use `summary()` for what the run means: which folds failed, what
#>   each one selected, and the estimate across them.

Each row holds one outer fold’s score in .metrics, the setting it chose in .selected, and every candidate (setting tried) its inner search scored in .inner_metrics. ?nested_tune_grid describes each column.

summary() says in words how much of the design ran, what each fold chose, and the estimate.

summary(res)
#> 
#> ── Nested cross-validation results ────────────────────────────────────
#> Outer resamples: 5-fold cross-validation
#> Outer folds: 5 requested, 5 completed
#> 
#> ── Selected parameters ──
#> 
#> Selecting metric: rmse
#> ! mtry: 8, 8, 5, 8, 5 (folds disagree)
#> ✔ min_n: 2 (all 5 completed folds agree)
#> 
#> ── Estimate (5 of 5 outer folds) ──
#> 
#> rmse (standard): 2.49
#> rsq (standard): 0.842
#> 
#> ℹ A nested estimate describes the tune-and-fit procedure. For a
#>   procedure chosen before seeing this estimate, it is the number to
#>   report for the model `nested_final_fit()` builds.

The estimate

collect_metrics() averages the outer scores. Each mean is the estimate for the whole procedure (tune, select, fit), and std_err is the standard error of that mean.

collect_metrics(res)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err
#>   <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 rmse    standard   2.49      5  0.447 
#> 2 rsq     standard   0.842     5  0.0293

With summarize = FALSE, we get each fold’s score instead.

collect_metrics(res, summarize = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 4
#>    id    .metric .estimator .estimate
#>    <chr> <chr>   <chr>          <dbl>
#>  1 Fold1 rmse    standard       1.23 
#>  2 Fold1 rsq     standard       0.911
#>  3 Fold2 rmse    standard       3.22 
#>  4 Fold2 rsq     standard       0.819
#>  5 Fold3 rmse    standard       2.48 
#>  6 Fold3 rsq     standard       0.805
#>  7 Fold4 rmse    standard       1.83 
#>  8 Fold4 rsq     standard       0.766
#>  9 Fold5 rmse    standard       3.69 
#> 10 Fold5 rsq     standard       0.911

vignette("estimate") explains what this number describes and what to report.

The selections

collect_selections() stacks what each fold chose, with the fold label beside each row. agreement() counts how many folds chose each setting.

collect_selections(res)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>   id     mtry min_n .config        
#>   <chr> <int> <int> <chr>          
#> 1 Fold1     8     2 pre0_mod5_post0
#> 2 Fold2     8     2 pre0_mod5_post0
#> 3 Fold3     5     2 pre0_mod3_post0
#> 4 Fold4     8     2 pre0_mod5_post0
#> 5 Fold5     5     2 pre0_mod3_post0

agreement(res)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>    mtry min_n     n  prop
#>   <int> <int> <int> <dbl>
#> 1     8     2     3   0.6
#> 2     5     2     2   0.4

When the folds agree, the data points to one setting. When they split, we read little into any one choice. The model to deploy comes from nested_final_fit(), which tunes once more on all the data, so its choice can differ from every fold’s. The estimate above is still the number to report for that model, because the same procedure made it.

collect_inner_metrics() stacks the inner scores of every candidate in every fold. Here is the first fold’s RMSE for each candidate, best first.

collect_inner_metrics(res) |>
  filter(id == "Fold1", .metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(mean)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 9
#>   id     mtry min_n .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err .config     
#>   <chr> <int> <int> <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>       
#> 1 Fold1     8     2 rmse    standard    2.85     5   0.419 pre0_mod5_p…
#> 2 Fold1     2     2 rmse    standard    2.87     5   0.435 pre0_mod1_p…
#> 3 Fold1     5     2 rmse    standard    2.88     5   0.446 pre0_mod3_p…
#> 4 Fold1     5    10 rmse    standard    2.88     5   0.510 pre0_mod4_p…
#> 5 Fold1     8    10 rmse    standard    2.89     5   0.497 pre0_mod6_p…
#> 6 Fold1     2    10 rmse    standard    3.09     5   0.548 pre0_mod2_p…

The predictions

collect_predictions() stacks each fold’s predictions on its assessment rows. On this design, every row of the data is predicted once by a model that did not see it.

preds <- collect_predictions(res)
preds
#> # A tibble: 32 × 5
#>    id      mpg .pred  .row .config        
#>    <chr> <dbl> <dbl> <int> <chr>          
#>  1 Fold1  21.4  18.7     4 pre0_mod0_post0
#>  2 Fold1  14.3  14.7     7 pre0_mod0_post0
#>  3 Fold1  16.4  16.1    12 pre0_mod0_post0
#>  4 Fold1  21.5  22.9    21 pre0_mod0_post0
#>  5 Fold1  26    25.2    27 pre0_mod0_post0
#>  6 Fold1  15.8  16.1    29 pre0_mod0_post0
#>  7 Fold1  15    15.0    31 pre0_mod0_post0
#>  8 Fold2  22.8  25.2     3 pre0_mod0_post0
#>  9 Fold2  18.7  17.0     5 pre0_mod0_post0
#> 10 Fold2  15.2  16.6    14 pre0_mod0_post0
#> # ℹ 22 more rows

ggplot(preds, aes(mpg, .pred)) +
  geom_abline(lty = 2) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_obs_pred()

The plots

autoplot() draws the selections by default, one panel per tuned parameter and one point per outer fold.

autoplot(res)

With type = "performance", it draws each fold’s score, with a dashed line at the estimate.

autoplot(res, type = "performance")

A fold that fails does not stop the run, and the functions above answer over the folds that completed. collect_notes() lists what went wrong in any fold, one that completed included. ?nested_tune_grid describes failed folds and the dplyr verbs that keep the class.
